note: fast path only; novelty status is set by the ADS-backed G2 judge

result.reason: The core arithmetic holds: f=0.10 gives -2.5 log10(0.90) = 0.114 mag, and for swarm temperatures of roughly 600-1000 K the 1-5 um excess is large, so the mechanism is consistent and the pattern is within an order of magnitude of a plausible noise floor for nearby K dwarfs. However, the method builds L_obs by integrating XP + 2MASS + SPHEREx, which adds the re-radiated waste heat back in and largely cancels the deficit it is meant to measure. In addition, the claim's 'integrated 1-5 um excess' disagrees with the method's blackbody-extrapolated total, and only a fraction of a cool swarm's emission falls in 1-5 um.

checks.note: Deficit: f=0.10 gives 0.114 mag; f=0.05 gives 0.056 mag; this matches the card. The swarm returns f*L* as heat. Taking T_d ~ T*(R*/2r)^0.5 for a Sun-like star, T_d=300 K sits near 1 AU and T_d~800 K near 0.14 AU, both physically allowed. Blackbody fraction falling in 1-5 um: at T_d=1000 K (lambda*T from 1000 to 5000 um K) it is about 63%; at 300 K (lambda*T up to 1500) it is about 1%. So 'D equals the integrated 1-5 um excess within 30%' holds only for hot swarms near 1000 K or above. Fractional excess at 4 um over a 5000 K photosphere, with f=0.1: about 1.3x photosphere for T_d=600 K, about 5% for T_d=300 K.

Deficit side: the 0.03-0.05 mag precision for isochrone luminosity prediction is optimistic. A 0.1 dex logg error maps to about 0.25 mag in L. Main-sequence evolution of FGK stars spreads L at fixed Teff. For K dwarfs, a 50 K Teff error (about 1%) maps to about 0.05-0.09 mag. A realistic floor is therefore ~0.05-0.1 mag for K dwarfs and worse for G/F dwarfs, giving roughly 1-2 sigma per star at f=0.1. IR side: for T_d of about 500 K or hotter, the excess is tens of percent to over 100% of the photosphere at 3-5 um, well above a few-percent photometric and photosphere-model floor. The IR excess can therefore serve as the primary gate, with D as a consistency test. SPHEREx saturation and single-epoch precision for Ks<11 sources are not known to me with confidence.

(1) L_obs as defined (XP + 2MASS + SPHEREx integrated) includes the waste-heat emission, so D=1-L_obs/L_pred is biased toward zero exactly when the hypothesis is true. The deficit must come from a photosphere-only fit (XP + 2MASS J/H, or XP alone with a model SED). (2) The claim uses the integrated 1-5 um excess while the method uses a blackbody-extrapolated total; these diverge strongly below about 800 K. (3) The edge-on confounder test relies on the absence of a W3/W4 cold component, yet a cool swarm would itself produce W3/W4 excess, so W3/W4 should be modelled rather than used as a veto. (4) The sample size of ~2x10^5 with parallax error <1% and d<200 pc is plausible but not verified.

Grey absorption, isotropic coverage and thermal re-emission conserve energy. Binaries being overluminous is correct. Interstellar reddening at E(B-V)<0.02 is small, and its chromatic slope is testable across XP.

estimate.pattern_size: Optical deficit 0.114 mag for f=0.10 and 0.056 mag for f=0.05. IR excess at about 4 um is ~130% of the photosphere for T_d=600 K and ~5% for T_d=300 K (5000 K star, f=0.1).
estimate.noise_floor: Isochrone-predicted luminosity: about 0.05-0.1 mag for K dwarfs (Teff, [Fe/H] and evolutionary-spread limited), worse for G/F dwarfs. SPHEREx 3-5 um relative to a photosphere model: probably a few percent for bright dwarfs, with saturation and calibration uncertain.
estimate.sample_needed: Per-star significance of D is about 1-2 sigma at f=0.1 and about 3-5 sigma at f>=0.2-0.3. Using IR excess above 5 sigma as the gate, ~10^5 nearby K dwarfs suffices for an incidence bound near 1e-5 for hot (T_d >= 500 K) swarms with f >= 0.1.
estimate.assumptions: Blackbody swarm at a single temperature; grey isotropic coverage; photosphere approximated as a 5000 K blackbody at 4 um; d<200 pc so extinction is negligible; spectroscopic Teff error ~50 K and [Fe/H] error ~0.05 dex; SPHEREx bright-star photometry not saturated (unverified).

result.revision_hint: Define the deficit from a photosphere-only fit (Gaia XP plus 2MASS J/H, with SPHEREx and WISE excluded) so the re-radiated heat is not added back into L_obs. Compute E as the total excess luminosity from a blackbody fit to the SPHEREx 1-5 um residual combined with WISE W3/W4. Restate the claim as D = E_total within 30%, and restrict the primary sample to K dwarfs, where the isochrone luminosity floor is smallest.

archives.name: IRSA SPHEREx Quick Release (map key spherex)
archives.access: boto3 unsigned S3 (signature_version=UNSIGNED), bucket nasa-irsa-spherex (us-east-1), prefixes qr2/ and qr3/; header range reads tested (2,880 bytes in 0.2 s); irsa_sia2 as an alternative listing route
archives.what_it_provides: All-sky 0.75-5 um spectral images in 102 bands (R~35-130). This is the only source in the map covering the 1-5 um excess term E at spectral resolution.
archives.gap: Quick Release products are calibrated images, not a source catalogue, so forced photometry on many images per star is needed for ~2x10^5 targets. QR photometric calibration may not reach the ~1-2 per cent stability needed for a 5 per cent excess (to verify). The bright-star saturation limit matters for d<200 pc dwarfs down to G~6 (to verify). Sky coverage of qr2/qr3 at query time is to verify. The 1-5 um band only captures waste heat at roughly T>500 K; cooler envelopes radiate mostly beyond 5 um.
archives.volume_estimate: Order 10^7 image cutouts (2x10^5 stars x ~100 band-exposures). At ~50-150 kB per row-range read this is roughly 0.5-2 TB of S3 range reads (to verify); best run in AWS us-east-1.

archives.name: ESA Gaia DR3 (map key gaia)
archives.access: astroquery.gaia launch_job_async against https://gea.esac.esa.int/tap-server (anonymous), table gaiadr3.gaia_source. Precomputed cross-match gaiadr3.allwise_best_neighbour (tested). gaiadr3.xp_sampled_mean_spectrum (to verify), or astroquery Gaia.load_data with retrieval_type XP_SAMPLED.
archives.what_it_provides: Parallaxes (parallax_over_error>100 selection), RUWE, G/BP/RP photometry, and XP spectra over 0.33-1.05 um (R~30-100) for the grey-versus-chromatic dimming test. Also provides AllWISE and 2MASS cross-matches archive-side.
archives.gap: Anonymous async results are silently cut at 50,000 rows, so queries must be chunked and checked against COUNT(*). Archive release 3.15 announced breaking changes. The XP blue end at 0.33 um has lower S/N, and XP calibration systematics at the few-per-cent level limit the absolute flux.
archives.volume_estimate: gaia_source selection ~2x10^5 rows, tens of MB. XP sampled spectra ~2x10^5 x 343 samples x flux/error, about 1 GB.
archives.licence: ESA Gaia data, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO (acknowledge ESA/Gaia/DPAC)

archives.name: APOGEE DR17 (map key optical_spectra)
archives.access: SDSS SAS file allStar-dr17-synspec_rev1.fits (download). CasJobs/TAP tables of ASPCAP parameters are listed in the map but table names are to verify.
archives.what_it_provides: Spectroscopic Teff, logg and [Fe/H], plus multi-visit RV scatter for binary rejection.
archives.gap: File-only access on SAS, so no archive-side join with Gaia without CasJobs (to verify). APOGEE dwarfs within 200 pc number only a few times 10^4 (to verify).
archives.volume_estimate: single allStar file, several GB (to verify)

archives.name: GALAH DR4 / LAMOST DR10 (map key optical_spectra)
archives.access: GALAH DR4 allstar FITS via datacentral.org.au; LAMOST DR10 catalogue via dr10.lamost.org (access path unclear in the map; exact file names to verify)
archives.what_it_provides: Additional Teff, logg and [Fe/H]. These are needed to reach ~2x10^5 dwarfs and for the two-survey parameter agreement test.
archives.gap: No tested access path in the map. The LAMOST low-resolution logg precision may be too coarse for the 0.03-0.05 mag luminosity prediction. Two-survey overlap shrinks the sample considerably (to verify).
archives.volume_estimate: GALAH DR4 allstar ~1 GB (to verify); LAMOST DR10 stellar parameter catalogue a few GB (to verify)

archives.name: IRSA AllWISE / 2MASS (map key irsa_ir, via Gaia cross-match tables)
archives.access: gaiadr3.allwise_best_neighbour on Gaia TAP (tested, 3 s). 2MASS via gaiadr3.tmass_psc_xsc_best_neighbour (to verify). IRSA TAP upload as fallback, with comma join + WHERE and DISTANCE in arcsec.
archives.what_it_provides: JHKs anchor points for bolometric integration. W3/W4 for the cold-component test used to reject natural disks.
archives.gap: Bright-star saturation in W1/W2 for the nearest targets.

archives.name: Bayestar19 3D dust (not in archive map)
archives.access: python dustmaps package, bayestar query (local map file; not a tested route)
archives.gap: Not in the archive map. Within d<200 pc, E(B-V)<0.02, so the map adds little; the XP chromatic slope test is the main extinction control.
archives.volume_estimate: map file of order GB (to verify)

result.volume_estimate: Result tables ~1-2 GB (Gaia selection + XP spectra + cross-matches). Spectroscopic catalogue files ~5-10 GB (to verify). SPHEREx cutout range reads dominate at roughly 0.5-2 TB (to verify), best executed in-region.
access_plan: Gaia TAP (astroquery.gaia, anonymous async): select gaiadr3.gaia_source with parallax_over_error>100, parallax>5, ruwe<1.2, phot_g_mean_mag<13. Join gaiadr3.allwise_best_neighbour and the 2MASS best-neighbour table (to verify) archive-side. Chunk by source_id ranges to stay below the silent 50,000-row cut and verify each chunk against COUNT(*).

Download APOGEE allStar-dr17-synspec_rev1.fits, GALAH DR4 allstar and the LAMOST DR10 parameter catalogue (several GB total, to verify). This is unavoidable because the map offers no tested TAP route for these tables. Match locally on Gaia DR3 source_id, keep dwarfs with two-survey Teff/logg agreement, and drop APOGEE RV-variable stars.

Retrieve XP sampled spectra for the ~2x10^5 retained source_ids with Gaia.load_data(retrieval_type='XP_SAMPLED') or gaiadr3.xp_sampled_mean_spectrum (to verify), in chunks of fewer than 5,000 ids. This is about 1 GB.

SPHEREx via boto3 unsigned S3: list qr2/ and qr3/, range-read FITS headers to build a WCS/band footprint index, then range-read only the pixel rows around each target. Perform forced aperture/PSF photometry per band, flag saturated or blended stars, and run in AWS us-east-1 to avoid moving ~1 TB.

Correct extinction using the d<200 pc limit (E(B-V)<0.02), with optional dustmaps Bayestar queries (not in map). Predict L from MIST isochrones given Teff, logg and [Fe/H]. Integrate XP + 2MASS + SPHEREx (+ blackbody tail) for L_obs.

Compute D=1-L_obs/L_pred and the 1-5 um excess fraction E with bootstrap errors. Flag stars with D and E both >0.05 and D/E within 30 per cent, then test grey versus chromatic dimming across the XP range and check W3/W4 for a cold component. Report counts and the sensitivity limit as an upper bound on incidence.
result.licence_notes: Gaia DR3 is CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO with acknowledgement of ESA/Gaia/DPAC required, so derived tables must carry attribution and share-alike. SPHEREx and AllWISE/2MASS are public (IPAC/IRSA, NASA). APOGEE, GALAH, LAMOST and Bayestar are public, but their specific licence terms are to verify.
result.scheduled_release: Gaia DR4 on 2026-12-02 (per archive map) would improve parallaxes and XP calibration for the luminosity prediction. A calibrated SPHEREx source catalogue or full data release: release date to verify. Euclid DR1-Foundation (Nov 2026) is not needed.
result.reason: All required ingredients are public now: Gaia parallaxes and XP spectra, APOGEE/GALAH/LAMOST parameters, and SPHEREx 0.75-5 um spectral images. However, SPHEREx is available only as Quick Release images needing ~10^7 forced-photometry cutouts, with calibration, saturation and coverage still to verify. Two-survey-agreement dwarf counts within 200 pc may fall well short of 2x10^5, so the 5 per cent deficit-versus-excess test can only be run on a partial sample at present.

confounders.name: Isochrone luminosity systematics (age, Teff zero-point, [Fe/H], alpha)
confounders.how_it_mimics: At fixed Teff and [Fe/H] the main sequence spans up to roughly a factor two in luminosity between ZAMS and turnoff. A 1 per cent Teff zero-point error alone shifts L by about 4 per cent. Spectroscopic logg errors of 0.05-0.1 dex propagate to 10-25 per cent in L. A young or metal-poor star with biased parameters therefore sits below the isochrone prediction and yields an apparent deficit D>5 per cent with no physical light loss. The card's assumed 0.03-0.05 mag precision likely ignores this age degeneracy.
confounders.exclusion_test: Not addressed by the card. Replace the isochrone prediction with an empirical estimate: L from Gaia parallax plus an IRFM or angular-diameter Teff. Require the deficit to persist when the age is marginalised and when APOGEE, GALAH and LAMOST parameters are swapped. Calibrate the D distribution on a control sample of interferometrically characterised dwarfs (threshold to calibrate on a control sample). Discard stars whose D is consistent with the ZAMS-to-turnoff width.
confounders.exclusion_data: APOGEE DR17 / GALAH DR4 / LAMOST DR10 overlaps; JMMC stellar diameter catalogue and interferometric benchmarks; Gaia FLAME parameters; MIST plus a second isochrone grid (PARSEC)

confounders.name: Starspots and two-temperature photospheres in active dwarfs
confounders.how_it_mimics: Spot coverage lowers optical flux more than infrared flux. Fitting a single-Teff model then leaves an optical deficit and an apparent 1-5 um excess that are physically coupled, so D roughly equals E. Magnetic inflation of K/M dwarfs also biases the expected radius-luminosity relation.
confounders.exclusion_test: Not in the card. Flag activity using four indicators: X-ray luminosity, Gaia RVS Ca II IRT activity index, TESS/ZTF rotation amplitude, and APOGEE/LAMOST emission cores. Exclude or separately calibrate active and fast-rotating stars. Test whether a two-component spot model fits Gaia XP plus SPHEREx as well as a grey screen. A residue remains for low-amplitude, pole-on spotted stars.
confounders.exclusion_data: eROSITA eRASS1 and ROSAT 2RXS; Gaia DR3 activityindex_espcs and vbroad; TESS and ZTF light curves; GALEX NUV

confounders.name: SPHEREx and WISE blending with background or companion sources
confounders.how_it_mimics: SPHEREx pixels are about 6.2 arcsec, so a background galaxy, red star or faint neighbour inside the aperture adds 3-5 um flux and creates E. Combined with an unrelated luminosity-model scatter in D, this can satisfy D~E within 30 per cent by chance.
confounders.exclusion_test: Not in the card. Check the neighbourhood with Gaia DR3 sources within about 15 arcsec and with deeper optical and near-infrared imaging. Require a consistent excess in unWISE/CatWISE W1-W2 with clean cc_flags (all zeros) and ext_flg=0. Inspect the SPHEREx PSF residual for extended or offset emission. Require consistency across independent SPHEREx exposures.
confounders.exclusion_data: Gaia DR3; Legacy Surveys DR10 / Pan-STARRS1 images; unWISE and CatWISE2020; AllWISE cc_flags and ext_flg; Spitzer IRAC archival images where available; 2MASS cc_flg

confounders.name: Photospheric model mismatch at 3-5 um
confounders.how_it_mimics: Synthetic atmospheres misrepresent molecular bands, especially for cool dwarfs and metal-rich K stars: CO near 4.6 um, H2O, and TiO/VO in the optical. These errors produce a structured 1-5 um residual that, extrapolated with a blackbody, looks like E. The same models can underpredict optical flux, adding to D.
confounders.exclusion_test: Not in the card. Build empirical photospheric templates by binning SPHEREx spectra of control stars in Teff, logg and [Fe/H]. Require the excess to be smooth and continuum-like rather than tied to molecular band positions. Compare results across PHOENIX, MARCS and Kurucz grids. Thresholds to calibrate on a control sample.
confounders.exclusion_data: SPHEREx Quick Release spectra of matched control dwarfs; WISE W1-W2 colour-Teff loci; IRTF spectral library

confounders.name: Large-grain (grey) circumstellar dust: extreme debris disks, dippers, collisional clouds
confounders.how_it_mimics: Grains larger than a few microns give nearly grey extinction, which defeats the card's chromatic test. Hot dust then re-emits at 3-5 um. Clumpy or inclined debris after a giant impact can occult the star and emit similar energy.
confounders.exclusion_test: The card's grey-versus-chromatic test does not exclude this. Look for variability, since dust clouds produce dips and infrared variability: Gaia epoch photometry, TESS, ZTF, ASAS-SN, and NEOWISE multi-epoch W1/W2. Look for a silicate or cold component at 12-22 um, and for youth indicators such as Li and kinematic association membership. A residue remains for static, optically thin, quasi-spherical large-grain envelopes.
confounders.exclusion_data: Gaia DR3 epoch photometry and phot_variable_flag; NEOWISE-R single-exposure database; TESS/ZTF/ASAS-SN; AllWISE W3/W4; GALAH/APOGEE Li abundances; moving-group catalogues

confounders.name: Unresolved companion distorting spectroscopic parameters
confounders.how_it_mimics: A cool M-dwarf or brown-dwarf companion adds 3-5 um flux, creating E. It also biases the composite-spectrum Teff, logg and [Fe/H], so the predicted luminosity is wrong and a spurious D appears. The card's statement that binaries only make stars overluminous ignores this parameter bias.
confounders.exclusion_test: The card's RUWE<1.2 plus RV check is partly adequate. Add Gaia ipd_frac_multi_peak and ipd_gof_harmonic_amplitude, non_single_star, Hipparcos-Gaia proper-motion anomaly, APOGEE VSCATTER from multiple visits, and Gaia rv_amplitude_robust. Low-mass, wide-separation or long-period companions can still escape these checks.
confounders.exclusion_data: Gaia DR3 gaia_source and nss tables; Hipparcos-Gaia catalogue of accelerations; APOGEE DR17 allVisit; archival AO/speckle imaging

confounders.name: Calibration and instrumental artefacts (Gaia XP, SPHEREx Quick Release)
confounders.how_it_mimics: Several artefacts can create spurious D or E: Gaia XP blue-end and edge calibration errors, bright-star nonlinearity or saturation, persistence, ghosts, cosmic rays, and preliminary SPHEREx zero-points.
confounders.exclusion_test: Not in the card. Require consistency across multiple SPHEREx exposures and spacecraft orientations. Require agreement with WISE W1/W2 and 2MASS photometry. Use Gaia G/BP/RP photometry as a cross-check on XP integrals. Apply magnitude-dependent corrections derived from control stars (threshold to calibrate on a control sample).
confounders.exclusion_data: Multi-epoch SPHEREx QR2/QR3 cutouts; AllWISE/unWISE; 2MASS ph_qual; Gaia DR3 phot_bp_rp_excess_factor

confounders.name: Underestimated interstellar extinction
confounders.how_it_mimics: Dust missing from the 3D map dims the star, producing D, but it creates no matching E.
confounders.exclusion_test: The card's restriction to d<200 pc plus the chromatic XP slope test is adequate. Interstellar dust cannot also supply the 3-5 um excess. Cross-check against a second 3D map and against diffuse interstellar band or Na D absorption in survey spectra.
confounders.exclusion_data: Bayestar19; Lallement/STILISM 3D maps; Gaia XP slopes; APOGEE DIB measurements

confounders.name: Edge-on protoplanetary or transitional disk / YSO
confounders.how_it_mimics: An inclined disk occults the star (D) and its inner rim emits at 3-5 um (E).
confounders.exclusion_test: The card's chromatic-slope test plus W3/W4 check is mostly adequate. Add the following: accretion and emission-line indicators (H-alpha, Br-gamma in APOGEE), Li and youth flags, membership in star-forming regions, and variability. Restricting the sample to main-sequence dwarfs within 200 pc further limits this.
confounders.exclusion_data: AllWISE W3/W4; APOGEE spectra; SIMBAD YSO classes; Gaia variability; star-forming region membership catalogues

confounders.name: Look-elsewhere coincidence in the D-E plane
confounders.how_it_mimics: Among about 2x10^5 stars, independent non-Gaussian tails in D and E will pair within 30 per cent for some objects purely by chance.
confounders.exclusion_test: Not in the card. Preregister the cuts. Estimate the false-coincidence rate by scrambling D and E across stars and by injection-recovery tests on control samples. Require the D~E significance to exceed this empirical null.
confounders.exclusion_data: The survey sample itself (scrambled pairings); matched control samples

result.dominant_confounder: Isochrone luminosity systematics (age, Teff zero-point, [Fe/H], alpha)
required_cross_matches: Gaia DR3 RUWE, ipd_frac_multi_peak, non_single_star, phot_variable_flag and epoch photometry
APOGEE DR17 allVisit VSCATTER and multi-survey parameter agreement (GALAH DR4, LAMOST DR10)
Interferometric or IRFM Teff/radius benchmarks (JMMC catalogue)
AllWISE W1-W4 with cc_flags=0000 and ext_flg=0; unWISE/CatWISE2020; NEOWISE-R multi-epoch W1/W2
Legacy Surveys DR10 or Pan-STARRS1 imaging for SPHEREx-aperture blends
eROSITA eRASS1 / ROSAT X-ray and Gaia activity index
TESS, ZTF and ASAS-SN light curves
SIMBAD object types for YSO, debris-disk and moving-group membership
Spitzer IRAC archival photometry where available
result.reason: The luminosity deficit D rests on isochrone predictions whose age, Teff zero-point and metallicity degeneracies easily exceed 5 per cent. Spotted photospheres, SPHEREx blending, photospheric model errors and large-grain grey dust can each produce a coupled or coincidental D~E pattern that the card's chromatic test does not remove. Empirical luminosity calibration, activity and multiplicity flags, multi-epoch infrared photometry and scrambled-pairing nulls can shrink these confounders substantially, but a residue remains for the dominant one, so the pattern is separable only in part.
